header: I count a department shown by its code alone, or by its name alone, as half an answer: DSP has near-identical names (six Plant Garage sections) and six codes shared by two different departments. This looks at the columns the model's SQL RETURNS and says so when only one of the pair is there. The pipeline then gives the model one chance to put both in. It is pure and deterministic: it reads the SQL, it does not ask a model.

symbols.name: outputColumnNames
symbols.sig: export function outputColumnNames(sql: string): string[] | null
doc: Returns the names of the columns the final SELECT returns, or null when they cannot be known (SELECT *, parse failure).

symbols.name: checkDepartmentColumns
symbols.sig: export function checkDepartmentColumns(sql: string): string | null
doc: null means fine (both, or neither, or unknown); otherwise it returns an instruction for the model.

symbols.name: checkDepartmentIdentity
symbols.sig: export function checkDepartmentIdentity(sql: string): string | null
doc: Two DIFFERENT departments can share one number (101, 103, 21000, 40017, 83002, 98902: an executive-only department and a non-executive-only one). Matching rows to each other on department_code therefore merges them: "executives but no non-executives under the same code" then wrongly drops BLAST FURNACE (OPERATION) because a different department with the same number has non-executives. I compare departments by department_id (a department ROW), never by number alone. I judge only comparisons BETWEEN TWO COLUMNS; filtering on a list of codes is fine.
